newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Sprint on Global One partnership.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Sprint on Global One partnership.

text.p: Sprint Corp on Tuesday said it does not envisage offering an equity stake in Sprint to any Asian partner which joins its Global One alliance with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG
"We haven't seen the need to increase that equity," Kevin Brauer, president of Sprint Business told Reuters. "Remember we have a standstill agreement with our European partners."
The French and German partners each have a 10 percent stake in Sprint, and the alliance is scrambling to secure the best Asian partners before its archrival Concert.
Concert is the name for British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp, which agreed to merge in November.
The standstill agreement limits the ability of Sprint to issue new shares without the permission of its partners.

Brauer declined to say which Asian partner Sprint is looking for, but analysts believe that both Global One and Concert want to get NTT Corp, the main Japanese national telephone carrier as a partner.
Brauer said he was confident Global One would meet the $1.3 billion 1997 revenue target, which follows annualised 1996 revenues of $800 million.
However he conceded that the company had exceeded 1996 budgets, though declined to say by how much or why.
Sources close to Global One told Reuters last month that the venture had lost $370 million, instead of the $250 million budgeted, in 1996 company and job cuts were expected.
"From the original budget that was put in, yes (we did exceed it)," Brauer said. He also said some Global One headquarters staff were being cut, but would give no details.
"The employees have been told today, I believe," he said.
Global One employed 2,900 staff at end-1996, and is based in Brussels where there is both a corporate headquarters with around two hundred staff and a larger European headquarters.
However Brauer emphasised that overall Global One would employ 500 more people in a year's time than it does now. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
